newsitem.title: USA: IMC Global to spend $100 mln for upgrades.
newsitem.headline: IMC Global to spend $100 mln for upgrades.

text.p: IMC Global Inc, which agreed to acquire the Western Ag-Minerals subsidiary of Rayrock Yellowknife Resources Inc, said it will be investing about $100 million over a five year period to upgrade the combined potash operations of both companies.

Western Ag-Minerals, with an annual capacity of 400,000 tons of potash, had fiscal 1996 gross revenues of $40.8 million. Its mine and processing plant are located in Carlsbad, N.M., adjacent to an existing 1.1 million-ton-a-year IMC Kalium potash mining and processing operation.
"This acquisition is an ideal fit for our plans to grow IMC's potash business in the Southwest," said Robert Fowler Jr, IMC Global president and chief operating officer.

"The close proximity of the two mining operations will significantly improve efficiencies at both locations and double IMC's muriate of potash reserves in New Mexico. Reserves of other potash ores will increase by more than 30 percent and the life of the combined mining operation will be extended to over 30 years," he said in a statement.

The increased mine life justifies a major upgrading of the mining operation and its processing facilities, he said. The $100 million upgrade will make the Carlsbad operation a more efficient operation, he added.
